clue.text: Dispensed with electric current for gas

parts.note: to dispense with staff is to sack them, i.e. to have fired them
AMP, short for ampere, the unit in which electric current is measured

explanation.surface: Someone did without the mains supply and used gas instead.
explanation.walkthrough: FIREDAMP is the explosive methane found in coal mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the miners' name for methane, a flammable gas collecting in pits.

clue.text: Many in combat on the steps

indicators.note: the word in tells us the number goes inside the word for combat

parts.note: a fight is combat
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A crowd of people are brawling on a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals such as L (50) are often clued as 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of stairs between landings.

clue.text: Trader resolved to keep back development

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it down and reform it, so the letters of the trader are rearranged

explanation.surface: A merchant decides to hold back expansion of the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard is to slow or hold back the progress of something.

clue.text: Window or door, nothing less over the sea in France

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another means it is written above it
less here means minus, so the letter for nothing is taken away from the door

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, i.e. nothing
MER is French for sea

explanation.surface: A choice between a window and a door in a house across the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window projecting from a sloping roof.

clue.text: Overall scheme for teacher to design

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
a plan is a design

explanation.surface: A head teacher is given the task of drawing up a grand strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: A master plan is a comprehensive strategy covering every part of an undertaking.

clue.text: Be promoted to increase production

definitions.meaning: to rise to a higher rank or level
to raise output, as a factory does

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both moving up a grade at work and boosting the rate of manufacture.

clue.text: Deceitful pair stood opposite

parts.note: a pair is two
to face something is to stand opposite it

explanation.surface: A treacherous couple stood across from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with two faces shows one to you and another behind your back: hypocritical.

clue.text: Father I name with a bird, a conceited person

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Dad, a vain man, introduces himself as a bird-lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, foppish person, originally a word for a parrot.

clue.text: Produces a picture of the harbour lights

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: An artist paints the lamps of a harbour at night.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them in art or words.

clue.text: Hobby for fun as profit

definitions.meaning: money earned on savings or a loan

explanation.surface: Someone's pastime is enjoyable and lucrative too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a leisure pursuit and the return paid on capital.

clue.text: Hat that beats everything else

definitions.meaning: something that tops all the rest

explanation.surface: A piece of headgear outclasses all competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is called a topper, and anything that outdoes all others is also one.

clue.text: Centaurs!

parts.note: these mythical creatures are part horse, part man

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark hints at a pun: the word for riders also describes the half-horse, half-man beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurs are mythical creatures combining horse and man, and riders on horseback are called by the same compound word.

clue.text: The flag for a prohibitionist

definitions.meaning: a standard carried in a procession

explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag, and whimsically also one who bans.

clue.text: Remained unmoved yet rose to one's feet first

indicators.note: first tells us that the piece for getting up comes before the other

parts.note: stood up, i.e. stood
still means yet, as in 'still waiting'

explanation.surface: Someone stayed motionless, though they had got up from a chair beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand still is to stay motionless, without moving at all.

clue.text: Pay Cora the dispensing chemist

indicators.note: dispensing means handing out or distributing, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cora must be paid by the pharmacist who makes up prescriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispensing chemist' reads as one phrase, but 'dispensing' is the anagram signal on PAY CORA THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was an old-fashioned chemist who prepared and sold medicines.

clue.text: Destined never to be in good health?

definitions.text: Destined never to be in good health?

parts.words: Destined never to be in good health?
parts.note: read literally, someone fated always to be sick

explanation.walkthrough: The real meaning is doomed or unlucky; the question mark flags the literal reading of the two halves of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated means doomed to misfortune, and literally reads as fated to be sick.

clue.text: Sitting tenant who pays no rent

definitions.text: Sitting tenant who pays no rent

parts.words: Sitting tenant who pays no rent
parts.note: a sitting tenant is a legal occupier; here it is someone crouching who occupies a property illegally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting tenant' is a British legal term for an occupier with protected rights; the pun is on squatting as crouching.
explanation.definitionFit: A squatter occupies property without paying or having any right to it, and to squat is also to crouch.

clue.text: Dairy worker to exploit another amid confusion

parts.note: to milk someone is to exploit them

indicators.note: confusion signals that the letters of the little word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A farmhand takes advantage of a colleague in the chaos of the cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkmaid is a woman who milks cows on a dairy farm.

clue.text: Company might get wound up by him

definitions.text: Company might get wound up by him

parts.words: Company might get wound up by him
parts.note: wound up suggests a clockwork toy, but here means a firm being closed and its assets sold

explanation.walkthrough: To wind up a company is to close it down; the official who does that is appointed by a court or creditors.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquidator is the official who settles a failed firm's affairs and dissolves it.

clue.text: Medicine, a singular school subject?

indicators.note: a singular form loses the ending that looks like a plural

parts.note: physics is a science taught in schools

explanation.surface: Is medicine a single subject studied at school?
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an old word for medicine or a remedy, especially a purgative.

clue.text: Well-informed person was saucy

parts.note: ex means former, i.e. what was
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: Someone knowledgeable used to be cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is someone with specialist knowledge of a subject.

clue.text: Two boys shortly came to a full stop

parts.note: Hal is a short form of Henry
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A couple of lads quickly came to a stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to stop moving altogether.

clue.text: Sides from Liechtenstein sank out of recognition

parts.note: FL is the international vehicle registration code for Liechtenstein

indicators.note: changed out of recognition means altered until unrecognisable, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teams from a small Alpine state were sunk beyond recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanks are the sides of a body, an army or a building.

clue.text: It's enough to take one's breath away

definitions.text: It's enough to take one's breath away

parts.words: It's enough to take one's breath away
parts.note: the idiom suggests something amazing, but read literally it means stopping breathing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take one's breath away' usually means astonish; here it is literal suffocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphyxia is suffocation, a lack of oxygen from being unable to breathe.

clue.text: It is twice rejected by an artist

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the doubled word is turned round
twice tells us the little word is written two times

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist's work is turned down on two occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Like the days of one's youth perhaps wasted

definitions.text: Like the days of one's youth perhaps
definitions.meaning: describing a youth frittered away, as in the phrase about a wild youth

explanation.surface: Many remember their younger years as squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspent youth is a stock phrase for one wasted on idle pleasures; the word means squandered.

clue.text: Gathered skirt did take in sailors by the pound

indicators.note: take in means the word for sailors is held inside the word for did

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy
L is the symbol for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A dressmaker took in a skirt for navy men, charging by weight.
explanation.walkthrough: RN stands for Royal Navy, Britain's navy; L comes from libra, the root of the pound sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirndl is a full skirt gathered at the waist, from Alpine folk dress.

clue.text: Appeased at being put out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the word for being put goes around at

parts.note: placed means put somewhere
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was calmed down at being turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to pacify someone and stop them being angry.
